children: The recent regulatory draft on insurance commissions is harsher than expected, but insurance companies and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) remain attractive pockets of value, Ashwini Agarwal, Founder & Partner, Demeter Advisors, told CNBC-TV18.

The proposed regulations will impact earnings for distributors, including non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and banks. For banks, the earnings cut on a financial year 2026 basis is likely to be muted at a couple of percentage points. Strong credit growth, stable margins, and a benign asset quality cycle provide a buffer for the banking sector, leaving the stocks undervalued. Deeper cuts are possible for NBFCs facing asset cycle issues, Agarwal said, citing example of Bandhan Bank.

Expensive valuations kept Agarwal away from fintech names like PB Fintech, especially with early signs of regulatory shifts in distribution. Conversely, insurance companies present a compelling opportunity following a significant de-rating over the past three to four years.

"I'm quite constructive that this is probably the time to be buying insurance companies," Agarwal said. Valuations are attractive across both life and general insurance, with the economics of most general insurance businesses—particularly health—turning around, barring the loss-making third-party motor premium segment.

On the exchange side, the NSE remains a preferred pick over challenger BSE due to slightly better valuations. As a market leader and free cash flow machine, the NSE should trade at a premium or at least at par with its peers. Despite holding private shares in the NSE, Agarwal shares the regulator's valid concerns regarding futures and options speculation, particularly in the final half-hour of the last trading day. Managing this balance without severely impacting the exchange's large revenue stream remains a key monitorable.

Beyond exchanges and insurance, microfinance NBFCs offer reasonable growth and undemanding valuations. Most of these companies have recapitalised, and their cost-to-income ratios are expected to decline as asset books grow. Long-term opportunities also exist in smaller domestic chemical and pharmaceutical names that have not yet seen a strong re-rating.

title: Insurance stocks and NSE offer value despite regulatory risks, says Ashwini Agarwal
